consensus_decisions.decision: The shipped Bun kipc client cannot block: packages/@keld/kipc/src/transport.ts is a Bun.connect event-loop client with async receive() and one in-flight read. contested_decisions.question: What should happen when the Bun role does not answer a cancellable close in time (close-veto 'deadline expiry')?
contested_decisions.side_a: electron-maintainer: keep the window open, emit a diagnostic, close only when the Bun generation is actually revoked/dead; the host must never destroy a dirty document (draw.io preventDefaults every close).
contested_decisions.side_b: perf-engineer (round 1) / security-red-team (round 1): host proceeds and records ▲; revised perf-engineer: there is no host-side CALL deadline to expire at all — AppKit's windowShouldClose:NO and applicationShouldTerminate: terminateLater are async hooks and 02 §7's deadline is a frame-stall clock, not a reply-latency bound.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side A on outcome, side B on mechanism. The host never auto-closes (KEL-139 T1b forbids fabricated completion; Electron's own delegate returns NO and waits indefinitely). But 'suspending CALL deadlines' is the wrong frame: 02 §7:364-388 has no outstanding-CALL deadline to suspend; the timer that actually fires is the writer SO_SNDTIMEO once the parked Bun stops draining 8 KiB. The design is: async AppKit hooks on the host, window stays open, role health decided by link liveness/generation revocation, with a diagnostic.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Spike arm: windowShouldClose:NO + later programmatic close and applicationShouldTerminate: terminateLater + reply in a small objc2 harness with two windows, plus arm C (renderer never answers isModified → window stays open, diagnostic emitted, no 'closed' fabricated) and arm D (kill the Bun role while a modal is up → window survives, modal dismissed with typed error). Pass = ordering transcript matches Electron 44.4.5 on the same Mac.

contested_decisions.question: By what mechanism may the Bun main thread block for showMessageBoxSync (and later renderer sendSync's main-side reply)?
contested_decisions.side_a: perf-engineer and security-red-team: a worker-owned @keld/kipc transport (socket in a Worker, SAB ring + Atomics.notify, main thread Atomics.wait) that keeps draining the single link and replays EVENTs in order after wake; alternatively host-side per-role credit windows so the host parks its queue instead of its writer. One role, one link, one principal; a second HELLO is refused.
contested_decisions.side_b: electron-maintainer: the decision is open — either a Worker-owned SECOND authenticated link for the same role generation (an admission decision for KEL-75/KEL-97) or a visible refusal; E2 probes whether a stub host accepts a second HELLO for the same generation.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side A. A second link per role has no spec basis and would mint a second principal for one role (identity is link metadata, 02 §1/KEL-75:48-51), and it still leaves the primary link undrained while the main thread is parked. The worker-owned transport is the only candidate that addresses the measured 8 KiB stall, but it is a kipc public-API + wire-protocol gate (KEL-80 owner), not a facade detail; until it or credit windows land, showMessageBoxSync is SCAFFOLDED (typed KELD-COMPAT throw with fix-it) and draw.io's close-with-prompt step is a fail cell. Security-red-team's 'refused outright' is the right policy but was stated as fact where it is a design rule.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: perf-engineer's S0 two-arm fixture against the real @keld/kipc transport: arm A current main-thread transport vs arm B 150-line worker-owned transport, main parked 10 s while a second connection emits 100 × 64-byte EVENTs/s with host writer SO_SNDTIMEO=5 s; record bytes-to-stall, KELD-IPC-006 occurrence, in-order replay of ≥10k EVENTs with zero drops, and sync-CALL RTT (diagnostic). Arm C: credit frames in a keld-ipc test (frame.rs:46 already names the kind). Pass = B or C shows zero stall/zero IPC-006 and sync RTT within 2× raw kipc RTT.

contested_decisions.question: Which risk is the program killer?
contested_decisions.side_a: security-red-team (joined by electron-maintainer in round 2): the authority-model collision — if draw.io is config-only ONLY under legacy, the security unique never reaches the headline use case and legacy becomes the de-facto default.
contested_decisions.side_b: perf-engineer: 'Bun blocks ⇒ kipc link stalls ⇒ KELD-IPC-006' — measured today, reproducible, and sits on every editor's close dance; IPC hop latency is a chart problem with in-invariant fixes.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Both are real but of different kinds, and the evidence favors B as the first-proof killer: it is the only one with a reproduced measurement (park-probe) and it blocks primary_workflow step 4 for draw.io today. A is a program-level honesty risk, but it is already a labelled, sanctioned state (kel78: legacy is explicit with a printed forfeit; 'unverified' is the live state on every OS), so it narrows the claim rather than blocking the proof. Rank: (1) link-drain stall under blocking emulation, (2) legacy-only headline, (3) renderer sendSync mechanism on WKWebView (Zettlr-gated), (4) IPC hop latency (narrows claims only).
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: For B: S0 fixture above. For A: security-red-team's E1 Node-API tracer under Bun with a throwing @keld/electron stub, classifying every fs/net/spawn row on draw.io's activation + primary_workflow path as scopable or not; if most rows are scopable, a strict-profile node:fs facade spec is credible and legacy is a stepping stone, otherwise the headline is 'legacy-profile migration' and must be published as such.

contested_decisions.question: Where does the app's preload run — inside the trusted KEL-142 isolated WKContentWorld or in a third content world?
contested_decisions.side_a: electron-maintainer: same isolated world (authority-equivalent to Electron's trusted preload), with the contextBridge proxy enforcing Electron's value table so the raw handler/nonce cannot be re-exported.
contested_decisions.side_b: security-red-team: acceptable only if the value table is enforced AND KEL-142's page-isolation negative tests (kel142:376-384) are re-run with the preload present; a third world with a nonce-less relay should be costed because the preload can close over the raw handler, a leak path Electron does not have.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B's conditions are mandatory either way; the choice between same-world and third-world is open and cheap to test. kel142:224/249 keep the nonce and handler outside the page world; a preload sharing that world is new trusted code next to them. Do not decide on prose.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Arm G: a preload that attempts to exposeInMainWorld an object closing over the native handler or nonce → absent in page world; re-run every kel142 negative test with the preload loaded. Measure the third-world relay's per-call cost in the same fixture so the decision is cost-vs-isolation on numbers.

contested_decisions.question: Is Electron's main-process JS re-entrant during dialog.showMessageBoxSync on macOS, and therefore must Keld's parked-Bun model be ▲ or ✔?
contested_decisions.side_a: electron-maintainer: unknown — message_box_mac.mm uses [alert runModal] / [NSApp runModalForWindow:], an app-modal Cocoa loop; whether Chromium tasks/JS timers/IPC run inside it is undetermined; the two-dirty-windows Cmd+Q scenario is weaker than first stated.
contested_decisions.side_b: perf-engineer / security-red-team: Electron's documented semantics are 'block the process until the message box is closed', so queue-while-blocked replay is what Keld must reproduce.
contested_decisions.judge_call: [unknown]; the maintainer is right to withhold a mark. dialog.md says 'block the process' but a Cocoa modal run loop can still pump Chromium's message pump; the doc sentence does not settle re-entrancy. Record the Keld model as ▲ or ✔ only after the fixture.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: E3: Electron 44.4.5 fixture on a Mac — open showMessageBoxSync, fire a setTimeout and a renderer ipcRenderer.send during it, log whether any JS runs before the dialog returns; diff against Keld's non-reentrant parked model.

contested_decisions.question: How should draw.io's session.webRequest listeners (CSP header, file:// filter) be mapped?
contested_decisions.side_a: migrating-app-dev (round 1, via objections): statically compile the app's rules into host policy.
contested_decisions.side_b: electron-maintainer / security-red-team / perf-engineer: listeners are recorded no-ops (▲) only after the host enforces an equivalent — always-on CSP injection and loadFileURL:allowingReadAccessToURL scoped to the app code dir — proven by a negative control (file:// outside the app dir refused before bytes load); until then no-op widens read reach and is not a quirks flag.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B. The filters are JS closures over codeDir (electron.js 994-1023); compiling them needs a JS evaluator in the host, which violates one-parser/no-Electron-isms. The ▲ is conditional on the host containment landing with its negative control as an S1 Lane A gating artifact.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Conformance test: with draw.io loaded via file://, a request to a file:// URL outside codeDir fails before any bytes load under Keld; same fixture under Electron 44.4.5 confirms draw.io's own filter blocks it. Both must refuse.

contested_decisions.question: Which sync getters block Bun and which return thenables or mirror reads?
contested_decisions.side_a: migrating-app-dev (round 1): clipboard.readText and similar genuinely-blocking calls are blocking CALLs with deadline.
contested_decisions.side_b: perf-engineer: a getter blocks only when the corpus call site consumes the value synchronously (showMessageBoxSync at 876 does); draw.io awaits clipboardAction/windowAction (4497-4498), so a thenable return is a ▲ with the KEL-72 app.quit precedent; bounds/focus/maximized/fullscreen/displays/dark read a host-pushed ordered mirror (▲ one-event lag); boot-static values come from a pre-evaluation descriptor.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B, with the maintainer's addition that clipboard text can be a mirror refreshed on NSPasteboard.changeCount ([inference], unmeasured). Blocking is the exception decided per call site by keld migrate static analysis, because every block carries the link-drain hazard.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: keld migrate static-analysis output over draw.io listing each sync-API call site with 'awaited / consumed synchronously'; a conformance test that a thenable return at the awaited sites round-trips; mirror staleness measured as events between host state change and facade read under a 10k-event/s background stream.

kill_conditions.risk: Blocking emulation on the Bun main thread stalls the only kipc link: with the current Bun.connect client, a parked main thread stops draining the socket after 8,192 bytes of host→Bun traffic (measured), and 02 §7's 5 s writer SO_SNDTIMEO then yields KELD-IPC-006 (inference from spec). draw.io's close-with-unsaved-prompt depends on showMessageBoxSync, so this blocks primary_workflow step 4 for every editor in the corpus.
kill_conditions.experiment: S0 (1-2 days, scratchpad only): extend park-probe against the real @keld/kipc transport. Arm A current transport; arm B worker-owned transport (socket in Worker, SAB ring + Atomics.notify, main Atomics.wait for sync CALLs); arm C credit frames in a keld-ipc test so the host parks per-role queues at credit 0. In A/B park main 10 s while a second connection emits 100 × 64-byte EVENTs/s with host writer SO_SNDTIMEO=5 s; record bytes-to-stall, KELD-IPC-006, in-order replay of 10k EVENTs with zero drops, sync-CALL RTT (diagnostic only, no CI claim). Pass = B or C: zero stall, zero IPC-006, sync RTT ≤ 2× raw kipc RTT.
kill_conditions.fallback: If B passes: worker-owned transport becomes the @keld/kipc contract (wire-protocol + public-API gates), sync emulation allowed per KEL-127 (deadline, rate-limit, dev-warn). If only C passes: host credit windows land first (02 §7 planned work), blocking bounded by credit, not timers. If neither: showMessageBoxSync/sendSync are ✘ fail cells with fix-its; draw.io is re-scored 'config + 1 edit' (async showMessageBox in the isModified-result handler) and the program's promise becomes minimal-edit migration with a scored edit count. Refused: fake-async sync APIs, host auto-close on timeout, infinite host wait with no unhealthy-role signal, a second kipc link per role, moving window/close ownership into Bun.

contested_decisions.question: What mechanism, if any, lets the Bun main process block for showMessageBoxSync / sync reply without violating one-link-per-principal or killing the link?
contested_decisions.side_a: electron-maintainer: a Worker-owned SECOND authenticated kipc link for the same role generation ('sync sidecar link'), framed as an open KEL-75/KEL-97 admission decision; alternatively refusal.
contested_decisions.side_b: security-red-team + perf-engineer: ONE link whose reader moves to a worker for the whole session (SAB/Atomics mailbox to main; EVENTs buffered in order during a park and replayed after wake; never a second HELLO). perf-engineer also lists host-side credit windows as an alternative precondition.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B, with one correction. A second link for the same generation is a second principal mint (KEL-75 binds one link to one generation after HELLO) and therefore an architecture change by AGENTS' definition (principal minting) — REFUSED, not open. Credit windows alone are insufficient for a blocking CALL: they stop the writer from dying but the REPLY still arrives on a socket nobody reads while main is parked; they are needed for backpressure (02 §7 'later work', KEL-80 owner) but do not enable sync emulation. The worker-owned single-link transport is the only candidate and it is a @keld/kipc transport-ownership change requiring wire-protocol + public-API gates and an approved spec before S1's close veto or S3's sync dialog may land.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: perf-engineer arm B (150-line worker-owned transport against the real @keld/kipc frames; main parked 10 s while a second connection emits 100 x 64 B EVENTs/s; host writer SO_SNDTIMEO 5 s; pass = zero stall, zero KELD-IPC-006, in-order replay of 10k EVENTs, sync RTT within 2x raw kipc) plus security-red-team arm E (host issues generation-retire/quit CALL during the park; it completes within deadline, modal dismissed with typed error, window survives, no fabricated 'closed').

contested_decisions.question: What happens when a close-veto CALL to Bun exceeds its deadline?
contested_decisions.side_a: perf-engineer round 1 / security-red-team round 1: host proceeds and closes, records ▲.
contested_decisions.side_b: electron-maintainer (round 2, joined by security-red-team's fail-closed rung): window stays open, diagnostic emitted, role flagged unhealthy; host closes only when the Bun generation is revoked/dead.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B. draw.io preventDefaults every close and destroys only after the user answers; auto-closing is silent data loss and a fabricated completion (KEL-139 T1b). Electron's own delegate never closes without JS consent (windowShouldClose: returns NO). Record as ▲ 'close veto is deadline-bounded and fails closed; Electron blocks indefinitely'. Additionally per perf-engineer: the CALL deadline is not even the clock that fires today — the writer buffer is — so the rule to write is about backpressure plus lifecycle/revocation CALLs keeping their deadlines, not about suspending a CALL timer.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Spike arm C (renderer never answers 'isModified' -> window remains open, dev diagnostic, no forced close) and arm D (kill the Bun role while a modal is up -> window survives, modal dismissed with typed error, 'closed' not fabricated), transcript diffed against Electron 44.4.5 on the same Mac.

contested_decisions.side_b: perf-engineer: 'Bun blocks => kipc link stalls after 8 KiB => KELD-IPC-006' is the measured, reproducible first-proof killer; the authority collision is conceded but unmeasurable.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Both are right about different atoms and both gate. Under this lens the ordering is: (1) the parked-role/link-stall atom is the first-proof blocker because it is measured today and sits on draw.io's primary_workflow step 4; (2) the legacy-only collision is the program-level risk because its only fixes are a new spec (node:fs/child_process facades over brokers + OS sandbox) or accepting legacy as the headline, which erodes unique #2; (3) IPC hop latency narrows claims but has in-invariant levers. The maintainer's round-1 'host cannot wait on Bun' atom is dissolved by AppKit's async hooks.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: E1 (Node-API tracer under Bun with a throwing @keld/electron stub classifying every fs/net/spawn call on the activation + primary_workflow path as scopable or not) decides (2); the arm B/E spike decides (1); the registered two-hop RTT lane sizes (3).

contested_decisions.question: Where do boot-static values (app.getPath etc.) come from?
contested_decisions.side_a: security-red-team round 1: a static table sent at Ready.
contested_decisions.side_b: electron-maintainer + migrating-app-dev: available synchronously before the app module evaluates, from spawn env (KELD_APP_LINK precedent) or computed from declared identity.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B. draw.io constructs electron-store at top level (electron.js:30) and Electron documents pre-ready APIs as synchronous top-level calls. A Ready-time table would make the first corpus app fail at import. Values must be host-minted (identity stays host-owned) but delivered via the spawn contract, not a message.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Run draw.io's electron.js under Bun with a @keld/electron stub whose getPath throws unless pre-seeded; the import either completes or the failing call site is listed (part of E1).

contested_decisions.question: webContents.send to a destroyed or navigated target: drop with warning, or throw?
contested_decisions.side_a: migrating-app-dev (as quoted): drop with a dev warning for navigated/destroyed generations.
contested_decisions.side_b: electron-maintainer: webContents.send targets the CURRENT main frame (delivered after navigation, never dropped); after destruction the wrapper throws 'Object has been destroyed'; only frame-targeted paths (event.reply, senderFrame.send) go stale after navigation.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B for the destroyed case (consistent with MarkDestroyed-before-closed in base_window.cc) and for the navigation split (web-frame-main.md detached frames). The exact throw on destroyed webContents.send is [inference] from the shared destroyed-wrapper check; draw.io's ~17 event.reply sites ride the frame-targeted path and must bind to the sender's document generation.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Electron 44.4.5 fixture: call win.webContents.send after 'closed' and after a navigation; record throw text vs delivery; land as the conformance oracle for the sequence test.

contested_decisions.question: How should electron-updater / autoUpdater.setFeedURL be handled in the draw.io proof?
contested_decisions.side_a: perf-engineer: set DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true. migrating-app-dev (as quoted): facade throws unless the feed names the built-in identity. electron-maintainer: adapter emits update-not-available/error without authority.
contested_decisions.side_b: security-red-team: adapter accepts setFeedURL as a recorded no-op (▲ 'feed is host-declared; app feed ignored'), host-declared role env disables draw.io's own check, and a typed error is emitted only when checkForUpdates is actually invoked; never a fabricated update-not-available.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B. The env var only gates checkForUpdates; setFeedURL and property writes run unconditionally (electron.js:74-86, 2078), a throw is caught by safeUpdaterCall and surfaces a boot-time error dialog (92-141), and update-not-available without an updater is a fabricated effect (KEL-139 T1b). Role env must be host-declared in the role declaration, not inherited from the operator shell (186 utilityProcess ambient-env row). Updater real activation stays KEL-53.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Boot draw.io under the adapter with and without the role env; pass = no notifyUpdateFailure dialog, a ▲ row for setFeedURL, and a typed error only on an explicit checkForUpdates call.

contested_decisions.question: Does the app's preload run in the same isolated WKContentWorld as the trusted KEL-142 bridge, or in a third world?
contested_decisions.side_a: electron-maintainer: same isolated world, with the contextBridge proxy enforcing Electron's value table (functions proxied by id, prototypes dropped, Symbols throw) so the raw handler/nonce cannot be re-exported.
contested_decisions.side_b: security-red-team: acceptable only if KEL-142's page-isolation negative tests are re-run with the preload present; otherwise a third content world with a nonce-less relay.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Unresolved and cheap to test; I lean to a third world if any negative test fails with the preload present, because KEL-142's negative tests (:374-386) were written for a world without app code and 'deleting content-world isolation ... must fail a named test' is the standing contract. Authority-wise both equal Electron (preload is trusted app code); the question is leak surface, not authority.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Arm G: a preload that tries to exposeInMainWorld a closure over the native handler / nonce; pass = absent from page globals and request arguments, and KEL-142's six negative tests still pass with the preload installed.

contested_decisions.question: How are session.webRequest listeners (draw.io's CSP and file:// filter) mapped?
contested_decisions.side_a: migrating-app-dev (as quoted): statically compile the app's rules into host policy.
contested_decisions.side_b: electron-maintainer + security-red-team + perf-engineer: listeners become recorded no-ops (▲) backed by the host's always-on CSP injection and navigation allow-list (loadFileURL:allowingReadAccessToURL scoped to the app dir), with a negative control proving host policy is at least as strict as draw.io's filter; and this is a Lane A gating artifact for S1, not a quirks flag, because a flag may not no-op an app's security policy before the host enforces the equivalent.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B. The rules are JS closures over codeDir and request details (electron.js:994-1023); compiling them needs a JS evaluator in the host (an Electron-ism in core and a second policy parser) or silent omission. 03 §2/§3 already own CSP injection and allow-lists.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Conformance negative control: a file:// URL outside the app code dir fails before bytes load; a CSP header at least as strict as draw.io's is observed on the main document.

contested_decisions.question: For sync getters with no defining host event (clipboard.readText, windowAction), does the facade block or return a thenable?
contested_decisions.side_a: migrating-app-dev (as quoted): blocking CALL with deadline.
contested_decisions.side_b: perf-engineer: return a thenable where the corpus call site awaits the value (draw.io awaits clipboardAction/windowAction at 4497-4498), ▲ with the KEL-72 app.quit Promise<void> precedent; reserve a true block for sites that consume synchronously, 'decided per call site by keld migrate'.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B's outcome, Side B's mechanism rejected in part: a facade API must have one public return type, so tier-C getters return a thenable uniformly (▲, KEL-72 precedent) and `keld migrate` static analysis flags call sites that consume the value synchronously as scored fail cells with a fix-it; per-call-site return-type switching is not a stable contract. Blocking is reserved for showMessageBoxSync-class calls and only after the worker-owned transport lands.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: draw.io primary_workflow passes with thenable clipboard/window getters and zero sync-consumption sites flagged; any flagged site would be a visible ✘ row.

kill_conditions.risk: Bun cannot block without killing its link: a parked main thread stops draining the single kipc socket, the host writer stalls after 8 KiB (measured) and expires at the 5 s writer SO_SNDTIMEO as KELD-IPC-006 (inferred from 02 §7). Every editor's close dance (draw.io showMessageBoxSync at electron.js:876) depends on a block, so config-only editor migration is impossible without a transport change.
kill_conditions.experiment: 1-2 day scratchpad spike against the real @keld/kipc frames: arm A current main-thread transport; arm B worker-owned single-link transport (socket in a Worker, SAB ring + Atomics.notify, main Atomics.wait for sync CALLs, in-order EVENT replay after wake); in both, park main 10 s while a second connection emits 100 x 64 B EVENTs/s with host writer SO_SNDTIMEO 5 s; record bytes-to-stall, KELD-IPC-006 occurrence, 10k-EVENT replay order, sync-CALL RTT p50/p99 (diagnostic, no CI claim). Arm E: host issues a generation-retire/quit CALL during the park; must complete within deadline, modal dismissed with typed error, no fabricated 'closed'. Arm C (host side): prototype credit frames (frame.rs:46 already names the kind) so the host parks per-role queues at credit 0.
kill_conditions.fallback: If B passes: worker-owned transport becomes the @keld/kipc contract under wire-protocol + public-API gates (KEL-80/KEL-97 owners), sync emulation allowed with deadline + rate-limit + dev-warn per KEL-127. If only credit windows pass: they land first for backpressure, but sync dialogs remain SCAFFOLDED (typed KELD-COMPAT throw + fix-it to showMessageBox) because credits alone cannot deliver the REPLY to a parked reader. If neither: showMessageBoxSync/sendSync are ✘ fail cells, draw.io is scored 'config + 1 edit' (async showMessageBox in the isModified-result handler), and the program's promise becomes minimal-edit migration with a scored edit count. REFUSED: second link per role, blanket deadline suspension, host auto-close on expiry, fake-async sync APIs, window ownership in Bun.

kill_conditions.risk: Authority-model collision: draw.io's main uses node:fs with renderer-supplied paths, child_process spawn/execFile, and ambient network, so config-only runs only under `legacy`; if strict never reaches the headline use case, pressure to make legacy the de-facto default erodes unique #2 (zero ambient OS authority).
kill_conditions.experiment: E1: Node-API tracer under Bun 1.4.2 with a throwing @keld/electron stub, running draw.io's activation + primary_workflow path (open via dialog, edit, save, close-with-prompt); classify every fs/net/spawn row as scopable to a dialog-minted grant, scopable to a declared role, or unscopable; count rows per class.
kill_conditions.fallback: Publish the first proof under explicit legacy with every unscopable call listed as a fix-it and `authority_profile: LegacySandboxOff` in every record (brokers correct, containment forfeited); open the strict path as its own approved spec (node:fs -> FsBroker facade, child_process -> declared role or ✘) consuming KEL-78/KEL-140/KEL-143; never auto-select legacy from Electron options (03 §2).

kill_conditions.risk: Renderer sendSync has no engine-portable blocking primitive on WKWebView (browser main threads cannot Atomics.wait; only a synchronous XHR to a WKURLSchemeHandler is a candidate), which kills Zettlr-class activation (6 sites at store construction).
kill_conditions.experiment: E4: WKWebView probe where page JS issues a synchronous XMLHttpRequest to a host scheme handler that forwards to Bun and returns; record whether WebKit services it from the WebContent main thread, the stall duration, and the rate-limit threshold derived from measurement.
kill_conditions.fallback: sendSync stays ✘ with a fix-it (to invoke) per KEL-127 — no silent async rewrite; Zettlr activation cell is `unknown`, not failed-silently; draw.io is unaffected (0 sites).

kill_conditions.risk: Running the app preload inside the trusted isolated WKContentWorld creates a leak path Electron lacks: a preload could exposeInMainWorld an object closing over the raw native handler or the per-document nonce that KEL-142 keeps outside the page world.
kill_conditions.experiment: Arm G: adversarial preload attempts to re-export the raw handler/nonce via contextBridge; re-run KEL-142's six page-isolation negative tests (kel142:374-386) with the preload installed; verify the contextBridge proxy drops prototypes, proxies functions by id, throws on Symbol, and yields an empty object for the full ipcRenderer (Electron's documented table).
kill_conditions.fallback: Move the preload to a third content world with a nonce-less relay whose shape is no broader than window.keld.invoke (kel142 §5.1 relay rule); scoreboard ▲ for any contextBridge type-table difference.

kill_conditions.risk: Electron's mac sync dialog may let JS timers/IPC re-enter during Cocoa runModal; Keld's strictly non-reentrant parked-Bun model would then diverge in observable ordering for apps that rely on re-entrancy.
kill_conditions.experiment: E3: Electron 44.4.5 fixture on the same Mac: open showMessageBoxSync, fire a setTimeout and a renderer ipcRenderer.send during it, record whether handlers run before the dialog returns.
kill_conditions.fallback: If re-entrant: scoreboard ▲ 'sync dialogs are non-reentrant in Keld' with a sequence test; if not: ✔ for the parked model's ordering.

kill_conditions.risk: Close/quit veto sequencing with two dirty windows: Cmd+Q does not route through windowShouldClose (Apple), so a host that models quit as per-window close CALLs will mis-order before-quit / window closes / will-quit relative to Electron.
kill_conditions.experiment: 50-line objc2 harness: windowShouldClose:NO + later programmatic close for per-window, applicationShouldTerminate: NSTerminateLater + replyToApplicationShouldTerminate: for quit; two windows; transcript of hook order diffed against an Electron 44.4.5 run of the same fixture (before-quit -> per-window close -> will-quit -> quit; quitAndInstall inverts).
kill_conditions.fallback: If interleaving cannot be matched: host serializes close requests per app and the facade delivers them in order after the modal returns; ▲ 'window close events are serialized across a blocking dialog'.

rejected_ideas: A second authenticated kipc link ('sync sidecar link') for the same role generation so a Worker can perform a blocking CALL — it is a second principal mint; KEL-75 binds one link to one generation after HELLO and AGENTS defines principal minting as architecture; refused rather than left open.

Blanket suspension of inbound host->Bun CALL deadlines while a role is parked in a modal — would let an app defer quit ordering (KEL-139 AC6) and generation revocation (02 §7); also targets the wrong clock, since the measured failure is the writer buffer, not the CALL deadline.

Host proceeds and closes the window when a close-veto CALL times out — silent data loss for draw.io (preventDefault on every close) and a fabricated native completion (KEL-139 T1b); Electron's own delegate never closes without JS consent.
Atomics.wait on the Bun main thread while that thread owns the kipc socket — measured: 0 bytes drained during the park, host writer stalls at 8,192 bytes.

Host-side credit windows as a sufficient precondition for blocking calls — they prevent link death but cannot deliver the REPLY to a parked reader; necessary for backpressure, insufficient for sync emulation.
Facade answers checkForUpdates with a fabricated `update-not-available` when no host updater exists — fabricated effect (KEL-139 T1b).

autoUpdater.setFeedURL throws unless it names the built-in feed — draw.io's safeUpdaterCall routes the throw to notifyUpdateFailure, a user-visible boot-time error dialog; the divergence would be reported by the app, not the scoreboard.

Relying on the operator's shell DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE=true — the env var gates only checkForUpdates (setFeedURL and property writes run anyway) and role env must be host-declared, not inherited (186 ambient-env row).

Statically 'compiling' session.webRequest closures into host policy — requires a JS evaluator in the host (Electron-ism in core, second policy parser) or silent omission; use recorded no-ops (▲) plus host CSP/allow-list with an at-least-as-strict negative control.

A keld.compat.ts quirks flag that no-ops draw.io's file:// filter before the host enforces loadFileURL:allowingReadAccessToURL with a negative control — a flag may never widen authority; this is a Lane A gating artifact, not a toggle.

`keld migrate` emitting a wildcard `el:*` channel grant (as 03 §3's current example shows) — makes KELD-GUARD003 vacuous for the compat namespace when both corpus preloads hand the page arbitrary-channel send; grants must be enumerated and the spec example corrected in the same PR.

clipboard.readText (and other tier-C getters) as a default blocking CALL — draw.io awaits the value (electron.js:4497-4498); a uniform thenable with ▲ (KEL-72 app.quit precedent) avoids parking the loop.
Per-call-site switching of a facade API's return type by migrate static analysis — one public API, one return type; migrate flags sync-consuming call sites as fail cells instead.
Boot-static values delivered as a table at Ready/HELLO — draw.io constructs electron-store at module top level; Electron documents pre-ready APIs as synchronous top-level calls.

Dropping webContents.send to a destroyed target with a dev warning — Electron marks the wrapper destroyed before 'closed' and throws 'Object has been destroyed'; only frame-targeted replies go stale after navigation.
Running Electron's spec/ tree under Bun as the oracle, or copying its three-retry CI policy (research 214).
Publishing a close-veto RTT p99 from 1,000 samples — 01 §5.1 requires >=20 sessions x 100,000 calls with a session-block bootstrap; run it as a diagnostic only, add a registry id first.

Using token-count usage scans (e.g. Zettlr 'send 84', draw.io 'WebContents.replace 22') as denominator or lane-sizing inputs — grep of resolved call sites gives 35/49/6/186 for Zettlr and 9 webContents.send for draw.io.
Moving window ownership or the close decision into Bun, or an infinite host wait with no unhealthy-role signal — breaks unique #1 or hides a fault.
Quoting the reference doc's '~1 ms equivalent framework path' as an Electron IPC baseline — uncited; and extrapolating the Bun ext-host bootstrap PoC (53%) to any whole app.

Reordering the spine (#312) to put compat lanes ahead of KEL-139 tasks, or scoring the first proof as `strict` — kel78 says strict cannot be reported from documentation and `unverified` is the live state on every OS.

scores.reason: Most decision-useful revision: replaced an unmeasured assumption with a reproduced measurement (8,192-byte writer stall while the Bun main thread is parked; I reproduced it on Bun 1.4.2), identified the real fuse (writer SO_SNDTIMEO, not a CALL deadline), dissolved the 'host must block' risk with verified Apple hooks (windowShouldClose:NO, applicationShouldTerminate delay), added a sized S0 spike with explicit pass criteria (10 s park + 100 msg/s, zero stall, zero KELD-IPC-006, sync RTT ≤ 2× raw), two concrete arms (worker-owned transport vs credit frames, and frame.rs already names Grant), per-call-site sync classification grounded in draw.io's awaited clipboardAction, registered metric ids before publication, and corrected its own counts. Deductions: host-side KELD-IPC-006 consequence is inference (probe server was Bun, not the Rust host); in-order EVENT replay during a park and KEL-80 ownership of the worker design were raised by security-red-team, not here; 'credit windows alone' cannot give a blocking read, which the position does not state.

Highest-yield gating decisions: enumerated el:<channel> grants with el:* refused by migrate (grounded in both corpus preloads exposing arbitrary-channel send), child principals start with channels: [] (03 §3 line 243), scoped deadline rule (app-level CALLs only; lifecycle/revocation keep deadlines and fail closed), preload-in-isolated-world must re-run KEL-142 negative tests or move to a third world, updater as recorded no-op + host-declared role env (correct per electron.js:74-141, 2078), legacy proof framed as 'brokers correct, containment forfeited'. Experiments E-H have pass criteria and a refused list. Deductions: still models the hazard as a CALL-deadline to suspend rather than the writer-stall clock perf measured; Electron doc semantics not re-fetched (disclosed); the worker-owned reader is asserted as 'the only candidate' without the probe evidence; one receipt mislocates draw.io's webRequest block (it is at :994-1023, not ~1718-1760).

Strong on falsifiable Electron-semantics decisions, each verified: tombstone flipped before 'closed' (base_window.cc), boot-static descriptor before app-module evaluation (electron.js:30,58; app.md pre-ready sentence), webContents.send to current generation vs event.reply frame-bound, beforeunload ▲ with zero corpus demand, S3b promoted to a gate, honest changed_mind list. consensus_decisions.decision: The shipped @keld/kipc Bun client is Promise-based (Bun.connect data/drain callbacks, one in-flight readFrame); no blocking kipc read exists. Any synchronous main-process emulation (showMessageBoxSync, close veto reply, renderer sendSync main side) is an unbuilt transport-ownership change (worker-owned single reader + Atomics.wait mailbox) and/or host credit windows, owned by KEL-80 with wire-protocol and public-API review gates — never a facade detail and never a second authenticated link.
consensus_decisions.evidence: transport.ts:600-615,764-775,925-962 (verified); 02 §7 lines 364-388 'credit windows remain later work'; frame.rs:46 Grant kind unused; KEL-75 one link bound per generation; all three delivered revisions concede the maintainer's original 'blocking reader' premise was false.

consensus_decisions.decision: Parking the Bun main thread while it owns the kipc socket stops draining the link after exactly one 8,192-byte kernel buffer (macOS net.local.stream.sendspace); the host writer then stalls. Nothing that parks the Bun main thread may land before a transport design that survives this is proven (perf-engineer's S0 gate).
consensus_decisions.evidence: park-probe reproduced by the judge on Bun 1.4.2: acceptedBytes 8192, stalledAtBytes 8192, bytesSeenDuringPark 0; sysctl sendspace=recvspace=8192. [inference] stall → KELD-IPC-006 after the 5 s writer SO_SNDTIMEO per 02 §7 (host arm not yet exercised).

consensus_decisions.decision: Host-side close and quit vetoes need no blocking: windowShouldClose: returns NO and the host closes programmatically after Bun allows; app quit goes through applicationShouldTerminate with delayed reply. Deadline expiry keeps the window open (fail closed, diagnostic, role flagged); the host closes a window on its own only when the Bun generation is revoked. Host auto-close on timeout is refused as fabricated completion.
consensus_decisions.evidence: Apple windowShouldClose(_:) 'not called when a user quits'; applicationShouldTerminate may delay then reply(toApplicationShouldTerminate:); Electron's own delegate does the same (electron_ns_window_delegate.mm return NO; browser_window.cc prevent_default=true); KEL-142 §6 'no UI thread blocks on Bun'; KEL-139 T1b no fabricated completion; draw.io preventDefaults every close (electron.js:947-963). All three revised positions converge on keep-open.

consensus_decisions.decision: Destroyed-object contract: facade objects are host-minted (handle, generation) pairs; the tombstone flips BEFORE 'closed' is emitted so isDestroyed() is true inside a closed listener and getters throw the exact 'Object has been destroyed' text synchronously; destroy() skips close/beforeunload and guarantees closed; webContents.send targets the current main-frame generation (never dropped on navigation, throws after destruction) while event.reply/senderFrame.send bind to the sender's document generation and go stale after navigation.
consensus_decisions.evidence: electron_api_base_window.cc OnWindowClosed: MarkDestroyed() → FlushWindowState() → Emit('closed') (verified); browser-window.md destroy() and 'Object has been destroyed' (verified); draw.io uses event.reply at 15 sites and validateSender tolerates null senderFrame (electron.js:692-700).

contested_decisions.question: What mechanism gives Bun a blocking main-process call (showMessageBoxSync, sendSync main side)?
contested_decisions.side_a: electron-maintainer E2: a Worker opens a SECOND Bun.connect to the host with its own HELLO for the same role generation ('sync sidecar link'), main thread parks in Atomics.wait.
contested_decisions.side_b: security-red-team + perf-engineer: refuse a second link (one role, one link, one principal; identity is link metadata); instead move the single kipc transport into a Worker that owns the reader for the whole session, hands frames to main via SAB/Atomics, buffers EVENTs in order during a park and replays after wake; optionally host credit windows so the host parks per-role queues instead of its writer.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B. KEL-75 binds a link to exactly one host-minted generation after HELLO and 02 §1 makes principal identity link metadata; a second authenticated link is a permission-model change with no owner and would be refused at the gate, so E2 as written tests an unshippable design. Worker-owned single transport is the only candidate that also fixes the measured 8 KiB drain stall; credit windows protect the host but do not by themselves provide a blocking read, so they are complementary, not alternative.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: perf-engineer's S0 two-arm spike against the real @keld/kipc transport: arm A (current main-thread transport) vs arm B (~150-line worker-owned transport with SAB ring + Atomics.notify), each parking main 10 s while a second connection emits 100 × 64-byte EVENTs/s with host writer SO_SNDTIMEO=5 s; record bytes-to-stall, whether KELD-IPC-006 fires, in-order replay of 10k parked EVENTs with zero drops (security arm H), and sync-CALL RTT p50/p99 over 1,000 calls labelled diagnostic. Pass = arm B zero stall, zero IPC-006, ordered replay, RTT ≤ 2× raw kipc. KEL-80 owner signs the design before it leaves scratchpad.

contested_decisions.question: How does the host hold a window close open while Bun decides, and what happens on deadline expiry?
contested_decisions.side_a: electron-maintainer: host emits WindowCloseRequested as a kipc CALL and blocks the window's close on the REPLY; host suspends inbound host→Bun CALL deadlines while Bun is parked in a modal; expiry keeps the window open.
contested_decisions.side_b: perf-engineer (adopting migrating-app-dev): NSWindowDelegate windowShouldClose: returns NO and the host performs a programmatic close after Bun allows; Cmd+Q goes through applicationShouldTerminate with a delayed reply; no deadline suspension is needed because 02 §7's deadline is a frame-stall clock that a pending CALL does not trip; the real hazard is the writer stall.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B on mechanism (verified: Apple says windowShouldClose is not called on quit and applicationShouldTerminate may delay then reply; Electron's own delegate returns NO; KEL-142 §6 forbids UI-thread blocks). Side A's expiry rule (keep open, fail closed, close only on generation revocation) is adopted by all and is consensus. 'Suspend CALL deadlines' is dropped: it names a clock that does not fire and, if written broadly, lets an app defer revocation/quit (security-red-team arm E).
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: A ~50-line objc2 harness: two windows, Cmd+W on a dirty window → shouldClose:NO then programmatic close on allow; Cmd+Q → applicationShouldTerminate returns later, per-window close sequence, reply; transcript diffed against the same fixture on Electron 44.4.5 on the same Mac. Plus security arm E: while Bun is parked, a host generation-retire/quit CALL completes within its deadline, the modal is dismissed with a typed error, the window survives, no 'closed' is fabricated.

contested_decisions.question: Which risk is the program killer?
contested_decisions.side_a: security-red-team (joined by electron-maintainer): authority-model collision — if draw.io is config-only ONLY under legacy, the security unique never reaches the headline use case and legacy becomes the de-facto default.
contested_decisions.side_b: perf-engineer: 'Bun blocks ⇒ kipc link stalls ⇒ KELD-IPC-006' — measured, reproducible today, and on the canonical editor close dance; the authority collision is a program risk that no one-week experiment can falsify.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Both are real but of different kinds: the link-stall is a falsifiable kill condition with a cheap experiment and belongs first; the legacy collision is a decision (is a legacy headline acceptable for the first proof?) already answered by consensus (yes, explicitly labelled) plus a tracer (E1 Node-API trace classifying fs/net/spawn rows as scopable) that bounds the strict-path spec. IPC hop latency is a claim-narrowing risk, not a kill.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: S0 spike result (above) settles the first; E1 tracer under Bun with a throwing @keld/electron stub on the activation + primary_workflow path, producing the list of unscopable Node calls, settles how large the strict-profile spec is and therefore whether 'legacy headline' is a transient or permanent state.

contested_decisions.question: Where does the app's preload run on WKWebView?
contested_decisions.side_a: electron-maintainer: in the same isolated WKContentWorld as the trusted KEL-142 bridge script, with a require shim exposing the sandboxed-preload module map.
contested_decisions.side_b: security-red-team: same world only if the contextBridge proxy enforces Electron's value table so the raw native handler/nonce cannot be re-exported and KEL-142's isolation negative tests are re-run with the preload present; otherwise a third content world with a nonce-less relay.
contested_decisions.judge_call: Side B's conditional: start in the isolated world (authority equivalent to Electron's trusted preload), but the KEL-142 negative tests ('page world cannot access the isolated native handler'; 'raw endpoint/token/nonce absent from page') become S2 gating artifacts re-run with draw.io's real preload, plus a new test where a hostile preload tries to exposeInMainWorld a closure over the handler/nonce.
contested_decisions.what_would_settle_it: Security arm G: a preload that attempts to re-export the raw handler or nonce via contextBridge → absent in page world; if it leaks, move to a third world and re-run.

contested_decisions.question: What does webContents.send do after navigation or destruction?
contested_decisions.side_a: migrating-app-dev (as quoted): dropped with a dev warning for a navigated/destroyed generation.
contested_decisions.side_b: electron-maintainer: webContents.send targets the CURRENT main frame (delivered after navigation; throws 'Object has been destroyed' after destruction); only frame-targeted event.reply/senderFrame.send go stale after navigation.

kill_conditions.risk: Bun main thread cannot block without killing its kipc link: parked thread stops draining; host writer stalls after 8,192 bytes (measured) and expires at the 5 s SO_SNDTIMEO → KELD-IPC-006 (inferred) → role restart during the canonical close-with-unsaved-prompt. Every corpus editor needs a block (draw.io showMessageBoxSync on the close path; Zettlr sendSync at store init).
kill_conditions.experiment: S0 (1-2 days, scratchpad): extend park-probe against the real @keld/kipc transport. Arm A current transport; arm B worker-owned transport (socket in a Worker, SAB ring + Atomics.notify, main Atomics.wait for sync CALLs, in-order EVENT replay after wake); arm C host-side credit frames in a keld-ipc test using the existing Grant kind. In each, park main 10 s while a second connection emits 100 × 64 B EVENTs/s with host writer SO_SNDTIMEO = 5 s. Record bytes-to-stall, whether KELD-IPC-006 fires, 10k-EVENT ordered replay with zero drops, sync RTT p50/p99 over 1,000 calls (diagnostic only). Pass = arm B or C shows zero stall, zero IPC-006, ordered replay, sync RTT ≤ 2× raw kipc RTT.
kill_conditions.fallback: (1) B passes → worker-owned transport becomes the @keld/kipc contract (wire-protocol + public-API gates, KEL-80 owner), sync emulation allowed with deadline + rate-limit + dev-warn per KEL-127. (2) Only C passes → credit windows land first; blocking still needs a worker so sync calls stay SCAFFOLDED until B is redone on top. (3) Neither → showMessageBoxSync/sendSync are ✘ fail cells with fix-its; draw.io scored 'config + 1 edit' (async showMessageBox in the isModified-result handler); program promise becomes minimal-edit migration with a scored edit count. REFUSED: second authenticated link per role, fake-async sync APIs, host auto-close on timeout, infinite host wait, window ownership into Bun.

kill_conditions.risk: Config-only draw.io runs ONLY under legacy: the security unique never reaches the headline use case and legacy becomes the de-facto default (authority-model collision).
kill_conditions.experiment: E1 (≤1 day): run draw.io main under Bun with a throwing @keld/electron stub and a Node-API tracer; classify every fs/net/child_process row on the install + activation + primary_workflow path as scopable (dialog-minted path grant, declared role) or unscopable (ambient fs with renderer-supplied paths, execFile at electron.js:4413).
kill_conditions.fallback: Publish the first proof under explicitly declared legacy with every unscopable call listed as a fix-it and authority_profile LegacySandboxOff in each evidence record; open the strict path (node:fs facade over FsBroker + child_process → declared role) as its own approved spec. The headline wording must say 'brokers correct, containment forfeited' and never 'default-deny demonstrated for draw.io'.

kill_conditions.risk: Renderer-blocking sendSync has no primitive on WKWebView (browser main threads cannot Atomics.wait; only a synchronous XHR to a WKURLSchemeHandler might block). Kills Zettlr activation (6 sites), not draw.io (0 sites).
kill_conditions.experiment: E4: a WKWebView page performs a synchronous XHR to the host scheme handler which forwards to Bun and replies; record whether the WebContent main thread blocks and the RTT for Zettlr's config-provider get-config shape; rate-limit threshold derived from the measurement.
kill_conditions.fallback: sendSync stays ✘ with a fix-it to invoke; Zettlr activation cell = unknown; never a silent async rewrite (KEL-127, 02 §5).

kill_conditions.risk: A deadline rule written as blanket suspension lets an app parked in a modal defer host-owned revocation and quit (KEL-139 AC6 one ordered quit owner); written as none, every close dance fails.
kill_conditions.experiment: Security arm E inside the S0/AppKit harness: while Bun is parked in a modal CALL, the host issues generation-retire and quit; both must complete within their deadlines, the modal dismissed with a typed error, the window survives, no 'closed' fabricated.
kill_conditions.fallback: Scope: suspension (if any) applies only to app-level CALLs whose reply the facade owns; lifecycle/revocation CALLs keep deadlines and fail closed (window stays, role unhealthy, diagnostic). Recorded ▲ 'close veto is deadline-bounded and fails closed; Electron blocks indefinitely'.

kill_conditions.risk: App preload running beside the trusted KEL-142 bridge leaks the raw native handler or document nonce into the page world via contextBridge.
kill_conditions.experiment: Arm G: hostile preload tries to exposeInMainWorld an object closing over the handler/nonce; re-run KEL-142's 'page world cannot access the isolated native handler' and 'raw endpoint/token/nonce absent' tests with draw.io's real preload present.
kill_conditions.fallback: Enforce Electron's contextBridge value table (functions proxied by id, prototypes and non-cloneables dropped); if still leaking, move the preload to a third content world with a nonce-less relay; deleting content-world isolation must fail a named test.

kill_conditions.risk: Wildcard el:* grant plus page-world window.keld.invoke makes KELD-GUARD003 vacuous for the whole compat namespace; both corpus preloads expose arbitrary-channel send, so the guard grant is the only renderer→main boundary.
kill_conditions.experiment: Arm F: a page-world script invokes an el: channel outside the enumerated grant → KELD-GUARD003; migrate emitting el:* is the negative control that must be refused; a setWindowOpenHandler-allowed about:blank child starts with channels: [].
kill_conditions.fallback: If static analysis cannot enumerate channels for a dynamic dispatcher (draw.io's single rendererReq channel is enumerable; Zettlr's generic window.ipc is not), the recorder (03 §3 destination, not live) produces the list under keld dev and the manifest ships enumerated; el:* is never written.

rejected_ideas: 'Bun's kipc client is already a blocking reader (echo_call)' — false; transport.ts is Bun.connect with async handlers and one in-flight Promise read; retracted by the maintainer.

Sync sidecar link: a Worker opening a second authenticated kipc link with its own HELLO for the same role generation — violates KEL-75 one-link-per-generation and 02 §1 identity-as-link-metadata; an unowned permission-model change, refused at the gate.

'Host suspends inbound host→Bun CALL deadlines while Bun is parked' — targets a clock that does not fire on a pending CALL (02 §7 is a frame-stall clock); the real fuse is the writer SO_SNDTIMEO after 8 KiB; broad suspension would also let an app defer revocation/quit.

Host blocks a WindowCloseRequested CALL on Bun's REPLY — unnecessary (windowShouldClose:NO + programmatic close; applicationShouldTerminate delayed reply are async by design) and forbidden by KEL-142 §6.
Host auto-closes the window on deadline expiry — silent data loss on draw.io's always-preventDefault close path; fabricated completion per KEL-139 T1b.
Throwing autoUpdater.setFeedURL facade — draw.io's safeUpdaterCall → notifyUpdateFailure shows a user-facing 'Update Error' dialog on every boot; use a recorded no-op ▲ instead.
Emitting a fabricated update-not-available when no host updater exists — fabricated native effect (KEL-139 T1b).
Relying on operator-shell DRAWIO_DISABLE_UPDATE — env gates only checkForUpdates; autoUpdater properties and setFeedURL run unconditionally; role env must be host-declared by migrate.

Static compilation of session.webRequest closures into host policy — JS predicates over codeDir cannot be compiled without a JS evaluator in the host (no second parser/policy owner); no-op ▲ + host containment negative control instead.
Making webRequest listeners a silent no-op before host file:// containment exists — widens read reach; it is a Lane A gating artifact, not a quirks flag.
keld migrate emitting el:* — makes KELD-GUARD003 vacuous; the guard grant is the only renderer→main boundary for this corpus.

Blocking CALL as the default for sync getters (clipboard.readText etc.) — draw.io awaits clipboardAction/windowAction; a thenable (KEL-72 app.quit precedent) is correct; blocking is reserved for synchronously-consumed sites.
Static app.getPath table delivered at Ready — too late; draw.io constructs electron-store and calls app.getPath('userData') at module top level.
'webContents.send after destruction drops with a dev warning' — Electron marks the wrapper destroyed before 'closed' and method calls throw; only frame-targeted replies go stale.
Token-scan counts as denominator or lane sizing (Zettlr 'send 84', draw.io 'webContents.send 15', 'WebContents.replace 22') — resolved call sites only.
Publishing a p99 from 1,000 closes — 01 §5.1 requires ≥20 sessions × 100,000 calls with session-block bootstrap CI; run it as a diagnostic with a registry id first.

Applying the zero-steady-state-allocation rule to the Bun-side JS mirror — that rule binds host Rust kipc/event-loop/guard paths; the mirror's real cost is write volume into an 8 KiB buffer toward a possibly-parked role.
Quoting the reference doc's '~1 ms equivalent framework path' as an Electron IPC baseline — uncited.
Running Electron's spec/ tree under Bun as the oracle, or copying its 3-retry policy (research 214).

Treating the Cmd+Q-two-dirty-windows interleaving arm as the discriminating test — windowShouldClose is not called on quit (Apple), and Electron's sync dialog is app-modal; quit must be tested through applicationShouldTerminate.
Claiming the first proof demonstrates default-deny for draw.io — under legacy the Bun role has ambient fs/net/spawn; only 'brokers correct; containment forfeited' is honest.
A recorder-produced keld.permissions.jsonc as an S3/S4 input — 03 §3 v0: no dev-permissive profile and no denial recorder exist; it is a Lane D/E deliverable.
